title: SignalArtifact
$comment: Compiler -> SME. The definition of a filtered (dynamic) signal: 'evaluate this predicate against events from this feed; publish matches under signal_id'. Upserted at strategy deploy; idempotent by signal_id (no-op if the hash already exists; refcount bumped). signal_id MUST equal the content hash of (feed, feed_version, filter, normalization_version) -- see signal-id.md for the exact procedure. Raw-feed recording is never gated by this artifact's existence or refcount.

feed.description: The raw feed this filter evaluates against, e.g. 'sportradar.nba.pbp'.

feed_version.description: Schema version of the feed. A feed schema change produces a different hash, hence a different signal.

filter.$comment: A filter is a single AND-group -- the stateless leaf/AND subset of the trigger grammar (ConditionTree), never a tree. An OR at the filter layer is represented as two filters (two signals, two hashes), split by the compiler's normalization pass; see trigger-normalization.md. Same grammar, one implementation -- never a second dialect.
filter.description: AND of stateless, per-event conditions over the feed's fields. Same grammar as trigger conditions -- the stateless subset.

normalization_version.description: Version of the feed-parsing/normalization logic. A parser change produces a different hash, hence a different signal.
